comments.comment: Thanks for your interest and compliments for Singapore.   I agree with the question mark in the title of your video as to whether Singapore is the most militarized country in the world. The jury is still out because there's North Korea and Israel too. It's not just about military spending as a percentage of GDP. It includes the extent to which the country and society is galvanized and ready for military action.  To describe Singapore as "the most military, intimidating and fiercely strong" (1:04-1:09) and to liken it to a "Sparta of the 21st century" (1:09-1:12) may appear as flattery to some and exaggerations to others. Considering the fact that Singapore as a  small city-state with scarce natural resources and dwarfed by regional and global powers, I'm also not sure whether Singapore "by itself would be able to stand up to almost any country in the world" (2:54-2:57), some of which have nuclear capabilities. Nevertheless, international diplomacy and upgrading its military defence capabilities as a credible deterrence against foreign aggression, remain imperative for its survival.  I agree with you that Mr Lee Kuan Yew (LKY) and his first Defence Minister Dr Goh Keng Swee exerted a heavy influence on shaping Singapore's military strategy in the early years of the Singapore Armed Forces (SAF). However, they in turn were part of a generation who experienced the Japanese invasion and occupation of Malaya that included Singapore. Much of the strategy today, though forward-looking and far-sighted, had also been influenced by the painful lessons drawn from the fall of Singapore during World War II. It comes as no surprise that at 6.20 pm on 15 February every year, the civil defence public sirens in Singapore will sound off to commemorate the moment Percival signed the documents surrendering Singapore to Japan. Lest we forget.  Another minor point of clarification: Mr LKY didn't rule Singapore for just 20 years. He was Prime Minister (PM) of Singapore when the city state was granted full internal self-governance since 1959 right through full independence in 1965 until 1990, when he stepped down as PM to give way to his successor. So Mr LKY ruled Singapore as PM for 32 years. Others may contend that LKY ruled even more years, as he remained influential in the Singapore cabinet, after stepping down as PM to become Senior Minister and later Minister Mentor till his death in 2015.
